title: React Accessibility Core Check
description: Check your understanding of accessibility fundamentals, semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard navigation, accessible forms, and testing.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: Why is semantic HTML important for accessibility?

options.text: It gives browsers and assistive technologies built-in meaning

questions.explanation: Semantic elements provide meaning and behavior that assistive technologies can understand.

questions.prompt: When should a native `<button>` usually be preferred over a clickable `<div>`?

options.text: When the user triggers an action
Only when the app has no CSS
Only for links to other pages

questions.explanation: Buttons include keyboard and accessibility behavior for actions by default.
ARIA can describe roles, names, and states, but it does not add interaction behavior by itself.

options.text: The label text assistive technology uses to identify a control

questions.explanation: Controls need accessible names so screen reader users know what each control does.

options.text: Announcing dynamic content changes to screen readers

questions.explanation: Live regions can announce status updates that appear after initial render.

questions.prompt: Which are part of good keyboard accessibility? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Keyboard support for custom interactive widgets
Removing outlines from every focused element

questions.explanation: Keyboard users need predictable navigation, visible focus, and working interactions.

questions.prompt: What is the best way to associate a visible label with a form input?

options.text: Use a `<label>` connected by nesting or `htmlFor` and `id`
Put the label in a comment

questions.explanation: Native labels give inputs accessible names and improve click targets.

questions.prompt: Automated accessibility checks can find many issues, but they do not replace manual keyboard and screen reader testing.
questions.explanation: Automated tools are useful but cannot verify every interaction, focus, or screen reader experience.
